findings.claim: The switch case for values <= byte.MaxValue was removed from the unsigned integer writer, so values 128..255 now fall through to TryWriteUInt16 and are encoded as uint16 (0xcd) instead of uint8 (0xcc). This is unrelated to the generator crash requirement. It changes the wire format, making output larger and non-canonical. It could also break consumers or tests that expect compact encoding, or any code relying on a size computed for the uint8 encoding. It is a hidden, unrelated change in serializer runtime. It is not a direct memory-safety issue, but it is a wire-format regression that could affect size accounting.

receipt_plan.detail: Write the unsigned value 200 (and 128, 255) via MessagePackPrimitives.TryWriteUInt with base-built and head-built code, then compare the bytes. Base should produce CC C8 and head produces CD 00 C8. Also run the existing MessagePackWriter/primitive tests for uint encoding.
